title: Round 3 — your four changes, plus one defect I caught
lead: Space flips Before/After. The first point is a bug I introduced last round and found by measuring rather than looking — worth seeing even though it is already fixed.

items.title: The banner label was invisible on light themes

points.what: Last round's banner was pale amber text on a pale amber tint — 1.07:1 on Crème, 1.14:1 on Light. The words were there; they could not be seen.
points.fix: All three banners are now a solid status colour with black text — 9.7:1, 7.6:1 and 5.0:1, identical in every theme.
points.why:
Flip to Before on the Crème tab: DOWNLOAD INTERRUPTED is rendered, just not visible. On Midnight the same code measured 5.62:1, which is exactly why it looked fine in the screenshots I sent you — I was checking the theme where it happened to work.

It took two goes, and the first was wrong for an instructive reason. My first fix used white text on amber-700, which in stock Tailwind is a dark brown (#B45309) and would have scored 5.02:1. But this app remaps that name: globals.css:294 sets --color-amber-700 to a bright orange (#FF9800), where white scores 2.06:1 — still failing. I only caught it because I re-sampled the pixels after shipping the fix instead of assuming it had worked.

The version you are looking at uses the app's three constant status colours with black text, which measures 9.7 / 7.6 / 5.0. Black rather than white because white fails on two of the three.

Two things worth keeping: the screenshot rig's contrast report never sampled this element, so a clean contrast report is not proof of contrast. And a translucent strip cannot be made safe across six themes at all — it takes its final colour from whatever sits behind it. A solid strip can.

points.what: A running download now wears a green banner in the same shape as the other two, and all three are centred.
points.fix: Confirm the green, the wording, and the centring.
points.why:
Green while it moves, amber when it stops but can carry on, red when it stops and can't. The banner text is the state name itself — Downloading, and Verifying for the checking phase at the end of a download, which is a real phase you'll see on a big model.

A finished model still has no banner at all: no news is good news, and a banner on every row would stop meaning anything.

points.what: The detail line lost its state word — it was "Downloading… · 73% — 82.9 of 113.0 GB · part 3 of 4" wrapping onto two lines.
points.fix: The banner says the state, so the line below carries only numbers and fits on one.
points.why:
This is the "simplify a smidge" you asked for, and it is what paid for point 4: dropping the state word freed exactly the line that letting the quality text wrap costs, so the row is the same height as before, not taller.

One more trim available if you want it: the line still starts with 66% — while a progress bar sits directly underneath saying the same thing. Dropping it leaves 74.2 of 113.0 GB. I did not do this unasked because a precise number is easier to quote back to yourself than a bar is to read. Say the word and it goes.

points.what: The quality line no longer ends in "…" — it shows in full and wraps if it needs to.
points.fix: Confirm this is what "its own line" meant.
points.why: Last round I clipped it to protect the row height. You said no. The height came back from point 3 instead, which is the better trade — nothing is hidden and nothing got taller.

closing:
Confirmed and left alone

  • A2 — the damaged banner stays red. Yellow means "stopped, you can fix it"; red means "stopped, you can't".
  • B5, C6 — the pause round trip and the (i) explanation are as you saw them.

What happens next

If these four are right, the design is settled and everything from here is machinery you won't see until it works: the record written beside each download, the honest list, the disk-space fix, and Resume actually resuming.
